iconicAnchor.label: French Rococo salon decoration
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The integrated rooms and objects establish Rococo as an asymmetrical, curvilinear, intimate decorative system rather than a generic layer of gold ornament.

sources.title: The Rococo Style in Europe
supports: Rococo joined architecture, furniture, and ornament into light, intimate interiors organized by shells, scrolls, and asymmetry.

sources.title: The Toilette of Venus
supports: Boucher's painted surface demonstrates the powder palette, floating diagonals, soft flesh, foliage, fabric, and theatrical ease needed in the image grammar.

bundledReferenceRationale: The powder-blue salon is an excellent lead with gilded asymmetrical scrollwork, shell ornament, curved furniture, pastel upholstery, mirrors, and layered decorative surfaces; the full room remains readable at card scale. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/rococo-salon/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
